place_name: The Matcha Tokyo - Azuela High Street
review_text: April 2026 – Located at Cluster 1, Unit 2 of Azuela High Street in Lanang, The Matcha Tokyo is one of the first establishments to open in this new complex. It is easy to find, as it fronts the courtyard and the Eco-bike station, right near the Azuela High Street signage. First, be prepared for the price point as this is an expensive spot. Aesthetically, the store is stunning; it’s bathed in a clean stucco finish with beautiful wooden furniture and a sleek, curved cushioned bench that spans the length of the space. Form the menu, we ordered the Matcha Frozen Latte (₱280), Ube Matcha Latte (₱280), and Matcha Frozen Lemonade (₱205). While we are no strangers to matcha, we were genuinely surprised by the lack of balance in these drinks. Matcha Frozen Lemonade. This was the only drink we enjoyed, though primarily for the lemonade itself; the matcha felt more like a thematic garnish than a core flavor. Ube Matcha Latte. This was a total disappointment. It lacked any semblance of Ube – the iconic Philippine purple yam now famous worldwide, thanks to Jollibee. Instead, the drink was overwhelmingly bitter, reminiscent of blended ampalaya (bitter gourd). Matcha Frozen Latte. Unfortunately, the flavor profile was completely off. I understand the appeal of high-quality matcha, but this mixture was unpalatable. We struggled to understand the high 4.7-star rating. Perhaps we ordered the wrong items, but it was a disappointing nightcap. I noticed the store offers stickers to those who leave reviews; however, I prefer to provide an honest account of our experience. Additionally, the cleanliness left much to be desired. We sat at our table for quite some time while waiting for our drinks but used items from previous customers remained uncleaned the entire time. For a premium-priced establishment, the service and quality should be much higher. Overall, not the best matcha experience, and if this is the standard, maybe, we are not made for matcha.

place_name: The Matcha Tokyo - Azuela High Street
review_text: Tried this café and it’s a nice, simple spot. The place is clean and has a soft, aesthetic vibe—nothing too fancy, just comfortable and easy to stay in. The matcha is really good. It tastes natural and well-made, not overly sweet, and you can actually taste the matcha itself. It’s smooth with a slight earthy flavor, which makes it feel more authentic. The desserts are also okay—not too heavy, and they go well with the drinks. Overall, it’s a good place if you want decent matcha and a chill environment. Rating: 8/10

place_name: The Matcha Tokyo - Azuela High Street
review_text: I recently tried The Matcha Tokyo and was impressed by the quality of their matcha. The flavor was rich, earthy, and noticeably more authentic than the average café matcha latte, with a pleasant umami depth and just the right level of sweetness. The minimalist Japanese-inspired atmosphere also made the experience feel calm and inviting. While the drinks are on the pricier side and the serving size could be bigger, the quality of the matcha and overall experience make it worth trying for matcha lovers.

place_name: The Matcha Tokyo - Azuela High Street
review_text: If you are looking for a spacious and aesthetic spot to get your matcha fix, THE MATCHA TOKYO is definitely worth a visit. The atmosphere is top-notch: clean, modern, and very relaxing. They have an impressive selection of drinks, pastries, and even more substantial food options for those looking for a full meal. What We Ordered: Matcha Latte with Soft Serve: This was a standout. The matcha flavor was present without being overpowering, maintaining a decent ratio of tea to milk. Hojicha Latte: Another solid choice for those who prefer that roasted, earthy profile. Hojicha Panna Cotta: We really liked this! The texture was spot on, and the hojicha ganache pour perfectly balanced the light-flavored jiggling panna cotta. The Verdict: It is definitely on the pricey side, so be prepared for a bit of a splurge. However, between the quality of the ingredients and the beautiful environment, it feels justified for a treat. Pros: Excellent tea balance, beautiful interior, great desserts. Cons: Premium pricing. Will we be back? Definitely! It’s a great place to hang out and enjoy high-quality matcha.
